chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halabi, from his father, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who allowed another man to reside in his house for the duration of his life. He said: “It is valid for him, and he has no right to evict him.”
I said: “And for him and his descendants?” He said: “It is valid for him.”
And I asked him about a man who allowed another man to reside [in his house] and did not set any time for him. He said: “The owner of the house may evict him whenever he wishes.”

key_terms.أَسْكَنَ دَارَهُ: granted someone residence in his house
key_terms.مُدَّةَ حَيَاتِهِ: for the duration of his life

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on allowing someone to live in a house for life or without a specified term?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on granting residence in a house. If residence is granted for the occupant’s lifetime, the grant stands and the owner may not evict him; but if no term is specified, the owner may remove him whenever he wishes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5597 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Ahmad ibn Umar Al-Halabi from his father from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who allowed another man to reside in his house for the duration of his life.
Imam (as) replied: "It is permissible for him, and he does not have the right to evict him."

I asked: "Does this also apply to his descendants?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is permissible for him."

I then asked Imam (as) about a man who allowed another man to reside in his house without specifying any time period.
Imam (as) replied: "The owner of the house may evict him whenever he wishes."
